conversation:
Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 55 years old, male. I've been having some right shoulder pain for a few weeks now. It started after doing some work in my backyard on a bunch of different projects, and it just hasn't gone away. It's been really sore, especially on the outside of my shoulder, and it hurts when I move it.
Doctor: Could you describe the nature of the pain (e.g., sharp, dull, burning) and whether it radiates to other areas? Have you experienced any swelling, redness, or limited range of motion in the shoulder? Have you had any prior shoulder injuries or surgeries?
Patient: The pain is more of a soreness, kinda like a dull ache, and it's mostly on the outside of my shoulder. It doesn't really radiate anywhere else, but it definitely hurts when I move it, especially when I raise my arm. I have had some issues with that same shoulder before from playing baseball when I was younger, but nothing major. I don't remember any surgeries on it.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or consultations for this shoulder pain, and if so, what were the findings or recommendations?
Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging studies done for this yet, but my doctor mentioned looking at an X-ray and there was no fracture. They did say they might order an MRI since I've had some issues before. I'm not sure what exactly they're looking for, but I'm hoping it's nothing too serious.
Doctor: Have you experienced any weakness, numbness, or tingling in your right arm or hand? Additionally, could you describe any specific activities or movements that aggravate or relieve the pain?
Patient: No, I haven't experienced any weakness, numbness, or tingling in my right arm or hand. The pain is aggravated when I move my arm, especially when I raise it or do things like lift stuff, but it doesn't really bother me when I'm just sitting still. I've been trying to ice it and take some Advil, which helps a little, but it's still sore to touch.
Doctor: Have you noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in the shoulder when you move it?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in my shoulder when I move it. It just feels sore on the outside, especially when I raise my arm or do any lifting. It's been pretty consistent like that.
Doctor: Could you describe the exact location of the pain on your shoulder and whether you have any difficulty performing daily activities such as dressing or reaching overhead?
Patient: The pain is on the outside of my shoulder, kind of near the top where the arm connects, and it's been bothering me when I try to reach overhead or do any lifting. It doesn't really stop me from doing daily stuff, but it does make some things a bit uncomfortable, like putting on a shirt or reaching for something high.
Doctor: Have you had any recent imaging studies, such as an X-ray or MRI, of the right shoulder? If not, would you be willing to undergo an MRI to better evaluate the cause of your shoulder pain?
Patient: No, I haven't had any recent imaging studies of the right shoulder yet. I was told they looked at an X-ray and there was no fracture, but they might order an MRI since I've had some issues before. I'm willing to do that if it helps figure out what's going on.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area. It's just sore and tender on the outside, especially when I move it, but there's no visible inflammation or heat around it.
Doctor: Could you describe the specific movements or activities that trigger the pain the most, and have you noticed any weakness or limited range of motion in your right shoulder?
Patient: The movements that trigger the pain the most are raising my arm or doing any kind of lifting, especially with the projects I've been working on in the yard. I don't really have any weakness, but I do feel some limitation when I try to move it a certain way, though I can still move it pretty well overall.
Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arm or hand that could suggest nerve involvement?
Patient: No, I haven't experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my arm or hand. It's just the soreness in the shoulder, and my hand grip feels fine. I don't think it's related to any nerve issues.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area. It's just sore and tender on the outside, especially when I move it, but there's no visible inflammation or heat around it.
Doctor: Have you had any recent imaging studies of the right shoulder, such as an MRI or ultrasound, to evaluate the soft tissues?
Patient: No, I haven't had any recent imaging studies of the right shoulder yet. I was told they looked at an X-ray and there was no fracture, but they might order an MRI since I've had some issues before. I'm willing to do that if it helps figure out what's going on.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth around the affected shoulder area. It's just sore and tender on the outside, especially when I move it, but there's no visible inflammation or heat around it.
Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or fall to the shoulder that might have contributed to the pain?
Patient: No, I don't think I've had any recent trauma or fall to the shoulder that might have contributed to the pain. It started after I was doing a lot of work in the yard, but I don't remember specifically falling or hitting it. It just gradually started hurting after all the lifting and projects I've been doing.
Doctor: Have you experienced any night pain or pain that disrupts your sleep?
Patient: Yes, it does bother me a little at night because I sleep on that side, but it's not really keeping me up or disrupting my sleep too much. It's more of a mild discomfort that I notice when I shift positions.
